caption:
Lulu jumped straight into futsal after work, and his hamstring grabbed on the first sprint. ⚽

Touch and futsal are all short sprints, sharp stops and quick turns, so hamstrings and ankles do a lot of the work. Ten minutes is plenty to warm up: easy jog, leg swings, then a few short sprints with turns.

Hybi's tip: stand on one leg while brushing your teeth, 30 seconds each side. Hamstring work like single-leg bridges twice a week can help too, starting with low numbers.

A sudden grab in the back of the thigh or an ankle that keeps giving way is worth an assessment. Our Sydney CBD and Chatswood physios can help. Book online via the link in bio.
